text:
Re-read after 0.54.2. The confirm below still holds: the grounding block does say "provenance" in prose where the payload key is edge["resolution"] (query.py:258) - a synonym, not rot, and both words are the right ones in their place.

Why it went stale: this function gained one line. before_edit now carries knowledge_lag alongside map_lag - the ambient report that N coordinates hold stale knowledge nobody has answered. It rides the same three JSON surfaces map_lag does, by deliberate symmetry: freshness.py established that a map may lag but must never lag SILENTLY, and knowledge had the detection without the telling.

The briefing already showed staleness for THIS coordinate; what was missing was the repo-wide fact, which is what an agent needs to know it broke something elsewhere. Keep both: the per-entity flag answers "is what I am reading trustworthy", the ambient line answers "did I leave a mess".

knowledge_lag counts COORDINATES with unsuperseded stale knowledge, never rows. Counting rows makes a diligent repo shout forever, which is how a warning becomes something people scroll past.

author: agent
text:
Re-read after the payload work. Every long-standing observation below still holds and was checked: "provenance" in prose against edge["resolution"] in the payload is a synonym not rot, the knowledge list is still built through for_display with has_stale counting only unsuperseded entries, the <0.7 threshold and the inheritance walk are unchanged, and map_lag/knowledge_lag still ride together.

WHAT CHANGED, and the reason is that this is an AGENT surface. The briefing listed every caller. On prometheus, before_edit on DirLocker.Lock returned 53,534 characters - roughly 13k tokens for one pre-edit check - of which 36,677 was a 342-entry caller list and 15,947 was radius["direct"] repeating those same 342 qualnames at 100% overlap, measured. For a human, density is clutter you can skip. For an agent it is a budget you cannot.

Three properties now:

  RANKED - production before tests, then the caller's own fan-in, then
  qualname for a stable order. This is not cosmetic: Head.Init has 103
  callers of which 98 are tests, so the five that matter were buried at
  an arbitrary depth.

  BOUNDED - CALLER_CAP = 12. Lock went 53,534 -> 2,173 chars (-96%),
  Head.Init 19,053 -> 2,632 (-87%).

  VISIBLE - direct_callers_total, _shown and _tests ride alongside. A
  list that quietly stops at twelve is a sampled list, and this repo's
  own guard message says nothing is ever sampled silently. The counts
  also carry information the full list did not: "103 callers, 98 tests"
  is a fact about the entity.

radius["direct"] is gone, replaced by direct_count. The names live in
direct_callers; duplicating them was free cost.

TWO FIXTURE ERRORS WORTH NOT REPEATING, both found by falsifying rather
than by the tests passing. First, naming a function test_* inside m.py
proves nothing: is_test_entity classifies by PATH. Second, with files
named m.py and test_m.py the unsorted edge order was ALREADY
production-first, so deleting the sort changed nothing and the ranking
assertion passed on luck. The fixture now uses zz_prod.py and aa_test.py
so the natural order puts tests first and the sort has to do the work.

Also worth knowing: the whole 96% reduction landed with the suite green.
Nothing asserted on the size or completeness of these lists before
test_the_briefing_is_ranked_bounded_and_says_so existed.

author: cli
text:
Re-read again after the census. The ranked/bounded/reported properties recorded in the confirm below are unchanged in behaviour; what changed is that they are no longer implemented HERE. The ad-hoc CALLER_CAP and the hand-built total/shown keys are gone, replaced by a call to payload.rank_bound_report.

That matters for the reason the census existed: this function's version was the sixth copy of the rule. Five already existed and two of those reported nothing. A structural pin now forbids a seventh - no module outside payload.py may construct a `<name>_shown` key.

direct_callers_tests stays here on purpose: it is a fact about this entity, not part of the truncation rule.
